messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — acme (POC) wants a private/non-prod deployment in their AWS account. They prefer PrivateLink over peering for security reasons. Can we outline an access/checklist and confirm whether a Dedicated pool can be run inside their VPC or if we must use our endpoint service? cc @raj_se @olivia_neteng

raj_se: Short answer: we can do both patterns but PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is usually smoother for cross-account POCs — no route propagation or CIDR coordination. Need their region, VPC CIDR(s), and target AZs. Also whether they require model artifacts to be pulled from S3 or want an air-gapped bundle.

olivia_neteng: PrivateLink pattern we use: Redwood publishes an Endpoint Service (NLB) in our infra; customer creates an interface VPC endpoint in their VPC subnets. Traffic stays within AWS network and you can enable private DNS. Pros: no peering, less routing work. Cons: ENIs in their subnets (IP usage).

ben_acme: Region is us-east-1. VPC CIDR 10.2.0.0/16. We'll use private subnets in 3 AZs. We prefer not to open internet egress from subnets for security. We need details: SG rules, private DNS, and any NAT/S3 access for model downloads.

raj_se: Ok. Checklist I recommend to share with them (short):
- Confirm region + AZs (we have it: us-east-1, 3 AZs)
- Pick 1-3 private subnets (one per AZ) with free IPs for ENIs
- Create interface VPC endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce) for our endpoint service — we will give the service name
- Approve endpoint connection from our side (we accept)
- Allow outbound to our NLB IPs on :443 (SG) and enable private DNS if they want app domain resolution
- If subnets are fully isolated (no NAT), decide model bundle: S3 pull (requires S3 egress) or offline model transfer
- Provide an IAM principal or support tunnel for logs/metrics retrieval (we can share short-lived creds)

raj_se: Example commands (customer-run) for creating interface endpoint:```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-01234567 --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0a1b2c3d4e5f --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb subnet-ccc --security-group-ids sg-0abc1234
```
(They should replace service-name with the one we provide.)

olivia_neteng: SG rules we usually ask them to add to the endpoint SG: ingress tcp/443 from their app subnets, egress tcp/443 to our NLB (outbound). If using private DNS, the endpoint will resolve to endpoint IPs in each AZ. Also note: interface endpoints create one ENI per AZ/subnet — plan IPs accordingly.

ben_acme: If our subnets have no internet egress, can the endpoint still reach you? We don't want NAT.

raj_se: Yes — interface endpoints route directly to the service; no NAT needed for PrivateLink traffic. But model downloads from our S3 require egress to S3 endpoints or NAT. Options:
- Enable S3 Gateway Endpoint in their VPC (recommended) so instances/containers can pull artifacts privately
- If they want fully closed environment and we can't use S3, we can provide a pre-packaged model bundle for offline load (requires manual handoff).

olivia_neteng: For VPC peering option (only if customer insists): ensure non-overlapping CIDRs, update route tables for private subnets to point to peer, and ensure security groups allow traffic from peer CIDRs. Peering is more brittle across accounts and across regions — we avoid it for POCs unless they specifically want full L3 access.

ben_acme: How many IPs will endpoint ENIs use? We're tight on /20s.

raj_se: Interface endpoint creates 1 ENI per AZ/subnet (so 3 ENIs for 3 AZs). Each ENI uses 1 IP (plus some reserved). However, if they put endpoint in multiple subnets within same AZ it'll create one per subnet. Recommend reserving ~4 IPs per AZ for buffer. If they want Dedicated pool as in dedicated GPU nodes in their VPC (we can run our runtime in their account), that will consume more IPs for nodes and load balancers. For a small non-prod pool we advise /24 per AZ as a safe starting point.

ben_acme: Any TLS/certwork? We need to know hostname we hit and cert validation for our internal proxy.

raj_se: We will provide a private DNS name (e.g., api.redwood-private-prod.internal) you can opt into when creating the endpoint. TLS certs terminate at our NLB; the endpoint preserves TLS. You can verify with:```bash
curl -vk https://api.redwood-private.internal/health
```
Expect a 200 and our cert CN to match the provided hostname.

deploy-bot: Ticket #RDW-4521 created: "acme POC PrivateLink endpoint - presales network checklist" — assignee: raj_se — https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RDW-4521

maria_sales: Action items for us: 1) share the service-name and accepting account IDs (we'll provide), 2) send the checklist to acme with the CLI snippet + SG example, 3) confirm whether they want S3 endpoint or offline bundle. Ben — can you confirm S3 gateway endpoint possibility by EOD tomorrow? :slightly_smiling_face:

ben_acme: I'll check with infra and get back by EOD tomorrow. Thanks all!

olivia_neteng: One more gotcha: if they enable VPC flow logs or an ETP proxy, ensure MTU stays default (1500) — some proxies break large payloads for model downloads. If they plan to proxy egress, we should test chunked responses.

maria_sales: Great — tagging this as next steps on the ticket. I'll follow up after Ben confirms. :thumbsup:
